highlights.title: Why are more roofs not made of solar tiles?
highlights.summary: Solar tiles were touted as an attractive alternative to solar panels - why have they not taken off?
body: Some people in the US "still hate the look of solar", Kate Collardson acknowledges.

She would know. Collardson handles operations for the Solar Service of Colorado, a solar maintenance and inspection company. She's also held just about every other job in the industry, from installer to instructor.
For those that hate the look of solar panels, an alternative is a solar roof, where the tiles (or shingles) house solar cells, but look much the same as regular tiles.
This is especially important for historic buildings, where heritage rules limit changes to their appearance.

highlights.title: Anthropic launches free AI security scans for open-source projects
highlights.summary: Anthropic's offering to help open-source projects track down security vulnerabilities with a new service called OSS Scanner. It says open-source projects that opt-in will get "thorough, periodic security scans by our strongest models at no cost." That could mean open-source projects get alerted…
body: The new OSS Scanner service offers vulnerability reports from Anthropic’s “strongest models,” including Mythos.

The outputs of this opt-in vulnerability scanner will be fully model-generated, without human review or triage. This will enable faster and more frequent scanning, but means that it is possible reports will be incorrect or invalid. These reports will be generated by our strongest models (including Claude Mythos) to give open-source projects the largest defensive advantage.

OSS Scanner is far from the first AI bug hunting helper out there. AI tools have helped find some major security flaws in open-source software over recent months, like the “Copy Fail” bug that impacted nearly every Linux distro in May. At the same time, some open-source projects are struggling to keep up with the sudden onslaught of AI-generated bug reports, including Linus Torvalds and even Google.

highlights.summary: Georgia Hunter Bell has enjoyed quite the year, winning a hat-trick of gold medals at the World Indoor Championships, for England at the Commonwealth Games, and again for Team GB at the European Championships.
body: But British female track success in 2025 certainly didn't stop there. Sprinter Amy Hunt made headlines with a record four-gold display in the Europeans in Birmingham, while Dina Asher-Smith now tops the all-time medal table at the championships after winning her 11th, eight of which are gold.

Among other successes, Keely Hodgkinson claimed World Indoor gold in the 800m in March - in the second-fastest indoor time in history - and set a new British record at that distance in the summer, though she'd be pipped to gold at the Europeans after sitting out the Commonwealth Games due to muscle tightness.
"It's really cool. just being part of this era. It's really fun," Hunter Bell told Sky Sports.
"We all know each other very well. We all travel together, see each other a lot throughout the year, so it's fun to tune in and be like, 'Oh, Amy's racing tonight'.

highlights.title: After 4 Hours, Phantom Blade Zero Just Became My Most-Anticipated Action Game
highlights.summary: Phantom Blade Zero looks to carve out its own space among sword-slashing action games. It blends simple controls and intense parries with stylish wuxia animations to create one of the most anticipated non- GTA 6 games of the fall release calendar.
body: Action game fans have had no shortage of choice in 2026. Romeo Is a Dead Man spotlights blood-soaked hack-and-slash combat, Beast of Reincarnation offers Souls-adjacent parry-focused fighting, and Onimusha: Way of the Sword takes parrying to the extreme with a plethora of defensive options.

I played from the very beginning of the game until the end of its first chapter. Afterward, I was plopped into two separate boss fights, defeating one and losing against the other. Trading blows with Phantom Blade Zero ’s bosses was certainly the highlight of my time with S-Game’s ambitious martial arts game, though the moment-to-moment action in between those boss fights didn’t reach the same highs.

I played as Soul, an assassin being hounded by members of The Order, a shadowy organization he used to work for. Maybe it was the jet lag after a 16.5-hour flight, but I didn’t pick up on that context in the preview; I learned Soul was a John Wick-style assassin on the run when director Soulframe Liang mentioned it during a roundtable interview following the gameplay session.

highlights.title: 3 Questions: What is the best path forward for AI in academia?
highlights.summary: MIT Statistics and Data Science Center Director Alexander (Sasha) Rakhlin shares important considerations for departments and institutions.
body: With artificial intelligence capabilities continuing to expand, universities now face complex, urgent questions about how to navigate increasing challenges, as well as new opportunities. Much attention is now directed toward this, including an MIT report on AI and education published this summer.

A new essay from MIT Statistics and Data Science Center Director Sasha Rakhlin, the Distinguished Professor in Data, Systems, and Society, IDSS and Brain and Cognitive Sciences, synthesizes recent discussions and readings about how AI is changing academia — particularly mathematics, statistics, machine learning, and engineering. Here, focusing primarily on graduate research and education, he describes key questions that departments and universities need to think about, and how they can best work with AI going forward.
Q: What is changing in research, and why is it happening so quickly?

highlights.title: Daredevil Star Charlie Cox Confirms He's in an Unannounced Sega Game | NYCC 2026
highlights.summary: Daredevil star Charlie Cox has confirmed that he is starring in another video game, this one for Sega. Cox opened up about the project at New York Comic-Con 2026, telling IGN’s Jeffrey Vega that he’s completed recording for an as-yet unannounced Sega video game. “I did another one!
body: “I did another one! It doesn’t have a name yet,” he said. “I did a Sega one. I’ve done one since. It hasn’t come out yet. It was fun to do. It’s hard. It’s a whole different job, man.”
Cox went on to share a humorous anecdote about his experience working on the game, saying that the crew weren’t aware that he wasn’t American.

“I’m not sure what I’m allowed to say, but I showed up for it, and I met them for the first time, they asked me to do this game, and so I agreed to it. Then I had to do 40 hours or whatever it was, and I showed up for the first day, and I was like, ‘Hi guys, nice to meet you! How are you?’ And all of them went, ‘...oh, he’s English.’ They’d hoped, they’d wanted him to be American. But now I’ve got to do 40 hours of lines I’ve not prepared in an accent. Yeah, I think they thought I was American.”

This, at least, gives us one bit of information about his role in the mysterious game — he’ll be playing an American character (or at least, a character with an American accent), and it’s likely that his role will be central to the plot, given that he recorded 40 hours’ worth of lines for it.

highlights.title: ICE Emails Discuss Using Palantir-Supported Tool to Investigate Voter Fraud
highlights.summary: Documents obtained by Democracy Forward show that ICE looked into feeding voter roll data into the ELITE tool, normally used to identify targets for deportation.
body: As the Trump administration has carried out a nonstop effort to undermine the midterm elections this year, the Department of Homeland Security appears to have looked into whether it could use a Palantir-supported tool to track people it believes have voted illegally.

The revelation is found in a tranche of documents obtained through a Freedom of Information Act request and published this week by Democracy Forward, a legal advocacy group. As well as revealing that DHS officials have investigated over 150 nonprofit groups in search of evidence they’re helping noncitizens register to vote, the documents show how Immigration and Customs Enforcement is now central to federal voter fraud investigations.

More specifically, Homeland Security Investigations (HSI)—one of ICE’s two major components—is spearheading the effort to uncover voter fraud, with its Innovation Lab (known internally as iLab) developing tools for agents.

highlights.title: She Designed Meta’s New AI Logo. Then Came the Hate
highlights.summary: Jessica Hische knew working for Meta might upset some people. But she didn’t anticipate just how angry they would get.
body: Bay Area lettering artist Jesscia Hische knew that when she took a freelance gig to design the M logo for Meta’s new AI assistant Muse, it was bound to make some people angry. “AI is such a third rail, and Meta is such a third rail,” she tells me.

“For the past year, I pretty much have 2-4 payrolls in my account at any given time, which if you own a small business, you know is pretty precarious,” she wrote. She added that she had also invested $100,000 in Studioworks, an admin platform she runs for creatives, and $30,000 in Drawling, her art shop for kids in Oakland, where she hosts classes and workshops. “I have 4 people on payroll including myself, my mom, and two shop employees,” she added. Nothing she said seemed to help.

Another person responded saying, “Doing this job is like doing a hit for the mob, and being surprised later when the mob takes you out too.” Other users posted photos of Hische’s house and speculated about her wealth and finances.
points: Jessica Hische knew working for Meta might upset some people.

highlights.title: Charlie Cox on the Return of The Defenders — 'There Needed to Be Some Kind of Closure' | NYCC 2026
highlights.summary: Charlie Cox hit New York Comic Con today to join in the Marvel Television panel — jetlagged and just in from Dublin, but ready to talk the return of Daredevil for Season 3 of Born Again. And not just the return of the Horned One, but also his old teammates The Defenders.
body: "I think there needed to be a full circle with that story," Cox told IGN's Jeffrey Vega today after the panel. "There needed to be some kind of closure with it."

The Defenders of course originated in the Netflix Marvel era, where each character — Daredevil, Jessica Jones (Krysten Ritter), Luke Cage (Mike Colter), and Iron Fist (Finn Jones) — had their own series before teaming up for the 2017 Defenders season. Eventually those shows all came to an end, but when Cox and Vincent D'Onofrio showed up in the proper MCU, it seemed like only a matter of time before the street-level heroes would be reunited.

"And Marvel were willing and able to bring them back and have a lot of fun with it," the actor said of the quartet returning. "It was great. We're such good friends. We have a great time together. There's some really interesting, fun dynamics that the fans seem to love, so it was great."

Part of that fun, Cox joked, was Mike Colter "giving away spoilers non-stop" — referring of course to the actor putting some info on social earlier this year that he shouldn't have. "We had to ban him from getting sides on set!"

highlights.title: Ice-T on ‘Law & Order: SVU’s’ Longevity and Cultural Impact: ‘I’m on a Good Treadmill, and I Want to Stay on It’
highlights.summary: “Law & Order: Special Victims Unit” has been running since 1999, and Ice-T has been there since almost the beginning. The rapper turned a four-episode stint in the show’s second season into a permanent role as Detective Odafin “Fin” Tutuola.
body: Ice-T recalled being told he was the longest-running actor in U.S. television history after 21 seasons of “SVU.” He attributed the show’s staying power to the nature of the series: “First off, it’s a whodunit. Everybody loves a whodunit. Secondly, it’s not only entertainment; it’s also therapy.”

His co-star Mariska Hargitay created the Joyful Heart Foundation in 2004 to support survivors of sexual assault, domestic violence and child abuse. Ice-T described the thank-yous he has received from women who saw justice served on the show that they might not have seen in real life, and said he was proud to be part of something that has been so impactful.

Ice-T credits his musician background as helping him know how to interact with fans. Music is also where his passion still lies. “For me to be in films and television is fun, but doing music is a whole ‘nother thing because I write, produce and direct the whole thing.”

He and Hargitay branched out into another realm with a Capital One commercial that aired during the Emmys — which Hargitay hosted. It was something Ice-T had done before, but his co-star had not. Still, he joked that she was “the star of the show” while filming the spot.

highlights.title: How Oracle turns days of work into minutes with ChatGPT and Codex
highlights.summary: Across recruiting, engineering, and operations, Oracle turns specialist knowledge into fast, repeatable workflows with ChatGPT Work and Codex.
body: Over a hundred thousand employees across Oracle are using ChatGPT Work and Codex, from talent acquisition to Oracle Applications Lab to the IT organization. In each case, work that used to rely on specialists and take days can now be done by anyone and is complete in minutes. Recruiters skip days of market research, business users describe an outcome instead of hunting for a report, and technical leads build tools that used to take a full team months.

The talent acquisition team used ChatGPT Work to build a talent market intelligence tool that takes a job description, researches comparable roles, benchmarks compensation, and assesses the talent pool across relevant locations. The tool arms the recruiter with valuable information that they need going into a conversation with the hiring manager, information that previously took 2–4 days to compile.

“We’ve gone from zero to a hundred,” says Jan Ackerman, Senior Vice President and Global Head of Talent Acquisition at Oracle. “Now we’re able to sit down and prep for about 15 to 20 minutes using the tool that we’ve built using [ChatGPT] Work.”

body: Spoiler warning: This article reveals details from the third episode of The Celebrity Traitors, series two.

highlights.summary: From learning how to bake Southern biscuits in Georgia to tracking urban beavers in Seattle, these experiences will add excitement to any trip.
body: Airbnb Experiences can often be hit or miss. It can be a little risky, for instance, to learn about the New York City mafia with retired detectives (what if the mobsters find out?), or hike to the Hollywood sign with a bunch of comics (what if they’re not as funny as you hoped?). When done right, however, they’re a great way to explore a new city—or the city you call home—and get a unique perspective on the area. Not only do plenty of Airbnb Experiences give you the chance to chat with locals, but you’ll likely learn something new.

highlights.title: ‘One of one’: A’ja Wilson stands alone with record fifth WNBA MVP award
highlights.summary: Aces star wins record fifth WNBA MVP award. Wilson becomes first player to win three straight. Olivia Miles finishes second in MVP voting. A’ja Wilson fine-tunes her shooting touch following every practice.
body: On Thursday, she received a voice message from former US vice-president Kamala Harris congratulating her on redefining greatness leaguewide after she was named WNBA MVP for a third straight year and for the fifth time overall.

“Obviously, that is an honor,” Wilson said. “A woman of our history, and I’m so appreciative to be able to share that moment with her through the phone call and the message of her delivering that I won my fifth MVP.”
In addition to becoming the first player to three-peat, Wilson won the award in 2020 and 2022.
Commissioner Cathy Engelbert, Aces owner Mark Davis and team president Nikki Fargas accompanied Wilson’s mother, Eva, who presented her daughter with the trophy.

highlights.title: Google’s AI note-taking app transcribes your meetings completely offline
highlights.summary: Google has released an experimental note-taking app that can transcribe meetings and audio files entirely offline, as reported earlier by TechCrunch. The app, called Google AI Edge Foresight, is free to use and runs on macOS using the company's on-device EmbeddingGemma 2 model.
body: Google AI Edge Foresight uses an on-device model to process your audio and notes without connecting to the cloud.

Similar to AI note-taking apps like Granola and Wispr Flow, Foresight summarizes your meetings while providing a space where you can take your own notes. Google says you can jot down shorthand bullet points during your meeting, and the app will transform them into “polished notes” based on the information in the transcript.

Along with transcribing your meetings, Foresight has a built-in assistant you can use to ask questions about what you’ve heard. You can also connect local files to the app, which it can reference when answering your questions. Google says your files, meeting audio, and notes “never leave your computer.”
Google AI Edge Foresight is currently only optimized for Macs with Apple Silicon, but stands out amongst a growing number of AI note-taking apps by operating on-device.

highlights.title: Avatar: Seven Havens Premieres This Week — Here's When You Can Watch New Episodes
highlights.summary: Original creators Michael Dante DiMartino and Bryan Konietzko returned for the 2D series, which follows a new Avatar, Pavi, over 200 years after The Legend of Korra. That’s around 300 years after the events of The Last Airbender.
body: Seven Havens will be streaming exclusively on Paramount+, now under the Skydance banner. The full series is slated for 26 half-hour episodes, just like the good ol’ days. However, those episodes will be split into two “Books,” the Avatar version of seasons.

The first three episodes of Book 1 will premiere on October 9. Subsequent episodes will be released in batches every Friday, so all 13 episodes of the Seven Havens will be streaming by the end of October.

As mentioned, the series will be streaming exclusively on Paramount+. Previous Avatar shows have eventually been released on DVD and Blu-ray, but that seems less likely for Seven Havens in the current Paramount era.
As for what to expect from the show, Seven Havens follows the usual Avatar tradition by picking up with, well, a new Avatar. The star of the new animated series is a young earthbender named Pavi.

highlights.summary: It’s for the best that “Animals,” actor Ben Affleck’s sixth outing behind the camera, is being released directly to Netflix — not that this slick, pacy serving of all-star pulp couldn’t or wouldn’t hold one’s attention in the multiplex.
body: Kerry Washington, Gillian Anderson and Steven Yeun join the filmmaker in the ensemble of a pulpy Netflix outing that is most interesting when it's most cynical.

Well, good within legal limits: When Cecilia asks if they could possibly offer some work to her boyfriend, illegal immigrant Ramon (Luis Gerardo Méndez), Abigail briskly explains that doing so could endanger her husband’s campaign. Still, it’s Halloween, and she and Mark trust Ramon enough to take their son Denny (Christopher Woodley) out trick-or-treating with his own, while they attend to more important matters: more campaign prep for Mark, and an online tryst with an extramarital lover for Abigail. So when Mark gets a call from a malevolent mystery predator, claiming that he’s taken Denny and demanding a $7 million ransom, multiple streams of guilt come into play.

highlights.title: White House blocks Microsoft from foreign worker hiring program
highlights.summary: An international visa program has for years allowed US tech companies to hire highly skilled workers from abroad.
body: Microsoft and several other technology firms have been barred by the White House from hiring skilled international workers on a permanent basis through a widely used visa program.

Vice President JD Vance on Thursday accused Microsoft alongside other firms of committing fraud through the use of the H1b visa programme and a related process for workers from abroad to become permanent US residents.
Vance claimed that Microsoft, one of the most valuable companies in the US, has been effectively replacing American workers with "foreign indentured servants."
Microsoft said most of the H1b visas filed over the last financial year were for existing workers, who are paid the same as local staff.

highlights.title: 9 Legend of Zelda Side Quests Scarier than Any Horror Game
highlights.summary: The Legend of Zelda has never been particularly shy about depicting curses, ghosts, and the walking dead (or ReDead). Its optional side quests are where Nintendo tends to let all three run wild.
body: On the first day in Majora’s Mask ’s Romani Ranch, young Romani practices archery. She does so to prepare herself to fight something that her older sister, Cremia, insists does not exist. According to Romani, They come every year around the Carnival of Time to steal cows. The invaders — reportedly inspired by the Flatwoods Monster of West Virginia folklore — drift slowly toward the barn, from the wee hours of the morning until sunrise. If you fail to protect the barn from these ethereal, ominously quiet alien figures, Romani will be whisked away…then returned later, without her memories or cheery personality. Win, and that doesn’t happen. And you also get a bottle of milk.

highlights.title: Animals review – Ben Affleck’s dull Netflix thriller is lacking in bark and bite
highlights.summary: Actor-director’s listless LA-set crime thriller makes for a surprisingly anonymous effort and one that feels very similar to many other, better films. Ben Affleck has pushed through multiple Hollywood comebacks, at least one predicated on his facility behind the camera, directing Boston-based…
body: Affleck the actor is still fun to watch, especially playing a politician visibly straining to not look like one – a charismatic guy nonetheless laboring to resemble a narrative version who may be a little nicer and more down-to-earth than he really is. But despite employing ace cinematographer Robert Elswit, who shot Affleck’s The Town as well as There Will Be Blood, among many others, the look of Animals is pretty Netflix-y – slick, lacking in texture and ultimately a bit dull. In other words, Affleck has – presumably by accident – imitated his character. This is a movie that just wants to get the job done with frictionless likability, with seemingly no one inquiring about why.

highlights.title: A good friend brings her dogs when she stays with me. I kind of dread it. What can I do? | Leading questions
highlights.summary: People often forget social rules when dogs are involved, writes advice columnist Eleanor Gordon-Smith. But you’ll have to say something if you want things to change. A good friend of mine stays with me regularly when she comes into town.
body: Eleanor says: It sounds as though you’re in the jam we all get into when we try to smooth things over: you can have the social ease of pretending something is fine; or the outcome from confessing it isn’t, but not both simultaneously.

Obviously, your friend should have paid more mind to the possibility that you don’t see her dogs like she does. Using the bathroom in your house? The first rule of society is that other people’s preferences might differ from yours, and that matters for how you treat them and their stuff.

But bring a dog into the equation and some otherwise intelligent people seem to forget that. They’ll trail behind on a leash giving the choreography of an apology while their dog puts paws on tables, bounds excitedly up to frightened children or treats furniture and food the way they’re allowed to at home. I’m saying this as a lifelong Dog Person, for what it’s worth: there is not a muddy paw print in the world I mind if it means I am playing with a dog. But we must admit, some dog people give the rest of us a bad name by assuming everyone sees their dog the way they do.
points: People often forget social rules when dogs are involved, writes advice columnist Eleanor Gordon-Smith.
But you’ll have to say something if you want things to change.
A good friend of mine stays with me regularly when she comes into town.
Obviously, your friend should have paid more mind to the possibility that you don’t see her dogs like she does.
